title: oncall-handoff-notes-kai-wong
content:
Shift summary (2026-02-28 -> 2026-03-01):
- Oncall: Kai Wong (taking 18:00-06:00 PT). Handoff from Priya at 18:00.
- Major items: brief spike in 503s during model rollout window (~19:12-19:25 PT), increased latency on rtx-dedicated-pool-3 between 02:30-03:10 PT, one kv-cache OOM observed on prod-1 (node id p1-n12) at 03:02 PT.
- Customer impact: ~120 API requests failed with 503s during rollout; customers auto-retried, no long-lived outages reported. Post-mortem ticket: JIRA-INC-423.

Incidents and timeline:
1) 19:10 PT: Automated rollout to model v2.1 triggered. Canary step showed elevated error rate on canary (3/5 health checks failing). Rollout continued due to misconfigured gating (see MR linked). 19:12 PT error spike to 1.8% across region us-west-2, primarily 503s and 429 downstream. 19:25 PT: I paused rollout and rolled back to v2.0; error rate dropped back to baseline by 19:28 PT.
- Action: follow-up MR to add stricter canary gating and circuit-breaker thresholds (MR 512).

2) 02:30-03:10 PT: Latency increase on route /v1/chat/stream with tail latency 95p -> 1.1s (baseline ~420ms). Observed coincident high batch sizes on rtx-dedicated-pool-3. Autoscaler had delayed scale-up due to a spike in batch accumulation; pods were pending due to spot eviction churn.
- Temporary mitigation: manually scaled dedicated pool by adding 2 reserved instances; reduced queueing.
- Action: tweak autoscaler policy to reduce scale-down aggressiveness during low utilization windows; create ticket to investigate spot eviction handling.

3) 03:02 PT: KV cache OOM on prod-1 p1-n12 during a long-running generation (customer X). Process restarted automatically by systemd monitor. No request data lost due to request retry fallback.
- Runbook note: if OOM recurs, set KV_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS to 80% for that pool and schedule rolling restart off-peak.

Open tasks / playbook TODOs:
- Add unit/regression test for canary gating logic (owner: Maya).
- Update rollout dashboard to include canary gating boolean and failure counters (owner: Noah).
- Create clear SLA-communication template for customers when a rollout is paused/rolled back (owner: eng-comm).
- Investigate memory growth in kv-cache over long sequences; possible leak in kv-eviction logic. Add heap profiling snapshot job for prod-1 (owner: eng-serving-runtime).

Temporary procedures (for next oncall):
- If model rollout triggers >0.5% error rate in canary after 5 minutes: immediately pause rollout, set traffic to previous model, and notify release-owner + eng-sre channel. Document steps: https://redwood-confluence/internal/oncall-playbook#rollbacks
- If route tail latency 95p >1s for >10 minutes: check autoscaler status, pod scheduling events, and spot instance termination events. Manual scale: add 2 instances to dedicated pool and set pool-level batching limit to conservative values (batch max tokens -> 1024).
- KV-cache OOM: identify node, cordon and drain it for inspection. If OOM observed on >1 node, reduce KV_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS cluster-default by 10% and schedule rolling restart at off-peak.
- Elevated 429s: check rate-limiter configs (per-customer and global), inspect per-token billing spikes, and escalate to product if a customer caused the spike. Temporary throttle: enable emergency rate-limit for offending customer and open support ticket.

Runbook draft (common checklist) — quick reference:
- Alert triage:
  - Confirm alert source and scope (single pod vs. global).
  - Check recent deployments (console > rollouts) and any active MR referenced in alerts.
  - Check metrics: error rate, latency p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, KV cache eviction rate.
- Initial mitigations:
  - For deployment-related errors: pause/rollback the rollout; pin traffic to last good model; notify oncall-rotation and release owner.
  - For high-latency: scale dedicated pools, reduce batch sizes, enable prefix caching for routes with repeated prompts.
  - For OOMs: cordon node, collect dmesg and /var/log/syslog, capture core if present, then restart service.
- Escalation criteria:
  - If customer-visible error rate >1% sustained for >15 minutes -> page eng-sre lead and CTO oncall.
  - If outage affects >2 regions or >30% of requests -> executive bridge and customer success notifs.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Improve observability: add a live view for canary gate status and per-gate metrics (failures, latency, resource pressure).
- Consider a canary rollback automation: if gate breaches threshold for N consecutive windows, auto-rollback and create incident draft. Need to discuss with release-engineering.
- Add a tiny synthetic load test that targets KV cache eviction and long seq runs prior to major rollouts.

Links and refs:
- PM doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Model+Rollout+Guidelines
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-423
- MR with gating fix: gitlab.com/redwood/runtime/-/merge_requests/512
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123AB45/p1612345678000

Unresolved questions:
- Was the canary gating config intentionally set to lenient values last week or was that change accidental? Need to check MR history and ask release owner.
- Is there a clean way to distinguish spot vs. reserved node evictions in autoscaler logs? Add parsing helper to tooling.

Handoff checklist for next oncall (Kai -> next):
- Walk through the incident summary above and confirm MR 512 is in review.
- Check that the autoscaler tweak ticket is created (link expected in JIRA-OPS). If not, create and assign.
- Verify that reserved instances added last night are still healthy and not in pending state.

Misc: local commands I used during shift (notes):
- kubectl get pods -n prod --selector=app=runtime -o wide
- ./tools/observe --route /v1/chat/stream --window 15m --metrics latency,p95,p99,errors
- systemctl status runtime-service@p1-n12

End of handoff. Ping me (slack @kai) for any clarifications.
